description: Three structural gaps. (1) OWNERSHIP CONFLICT: the spec pipeline (behavioral-spec.md:21-23) routes Supabase rows → enrichOnChain → aggregate → JSON as if the landing-repo netlify dashboard-sync.js owns /dashboard.json, but project CLAUDE.md states /dashboard.json is rendered by a Dais-owned dashboard-sync job from anicca-dais + anicca-genesis instance-state and that Anicca/landing must NOT write dashboard.json. The spec adds an on-chain enrich + aggregate path without saying which of the two 'dashboard-sync' producers gains the chain-read responsibility, who owns it, and how the guardrail is respected. (2) revenue_by_source is listed as a signed/persisted field (R1 behavioral-spec.md:30-31, R10 behavioral-spec.md:63-64) and consumed in the UI, yet R9's type-check list (behavioral-spec.md:62) covers only tags/revenue_today_usd/log_feed — revenue_by_source is never type-validated, so a malformed object reaches the drill-down. (3) earn_src (the ranked figure's provenance) is added to the element (R1 behavioral-spec.md:31) but R6's UI render contract (behavioral-spec.md:52) surfaces only a net_worth_src indicator — the verified/unverified state of the RANKED revenue is invisible, so an unverified high-revenue row looks identical to a chain-verified one.

crossEvidence.note: landing-repo netlify function vs the Dais-owned static-file render job — two different 'dashboard-sync' producers, unreconciled

fix: Name which producer enriches+writes leaderboard and reconcile it with the no-direct-write guardrail; add revenue_by_source to the R9 type-check list; add an earn_src indicator to the R6 UI render contract.
